notes: Chosen hook 'KOREAN MODELS: 49.3% ON CHINA' (cover slide 01). Sub-scores: clear in 2s 6 (the number and 'Korean models' land fast, but 'ON CHINA' is cryptic and could be read as a trade or usage stat; 'built on Chinese models' is only explained on slide 02 and later); curiosity 7 (nearly half of Korea's models resting on China prompts a 'how' and 'which ones'); concrete number 9 (49.3% is the study's headline, in yellow and large); promise kept 7 (slides 02-03 and 04 deliver the 49.3% / 35.9% / 14.9% split, Qwen at 46.8%, and the rise from 1.2%; but the cover says 'Korean models' while the figure covers 1,845 Hugging Face derivatives from Korea-linked accounts, Jan-Aug, not all Korean AI or services. The caption states this limit, and slide 02 already says 'nearly half of AI models released by Korean developers'); reader stake 3 (no explicit what-changes-for-you, but this is a plus only and the hook is strong on the others). Slide 02 text matches post.json and the render fits. The 49.3% itself first appears on the next content slide, not on 02, which is fine for a cover. Label check: option 1 'number' is honest. Option 2 'myth-flip' is weak: no myth is stated and the line has no number, so it reads more like a plain claim. Option 3 'rivalry' is honest but misleading in emphasis: Gemma (14.7%) is ahead of Llama (13.8%), and Qwen vs Llama is not the story. Option 4 'reader-impact' is mislabeled: it is about app rankings, not about the reader, and it is the counterpoint finding, so it undersells the headline. Compared with the others, option 1 is the best: it is the only one with the headline number and the broadest honest promise.
